kʷékʷlom h₁ésti moy. tód tébʰyo dídeh₃mi.
English: I have a wheel. I give it to you.

gʰóstim ne linékʷmi. h₂ówim pékʷoh₂.
English: I do not leave the guest. I am cooking a sheep.

ph₂tḗr h₂éǵrey h₁ésti.
English: Father is in the field.

ǵʰáysom dʰéh₁m̥.
English: I made the spear.

gʰóstis dʰwéri stísteh₂ti.
English: A guest is standing at the door.

wóydh₂e. h₂ówes h₂éǵrey h₁sénti.
English: I have seen them. The sheep are in the field.

h₁n̥gʷnís dʰégʷʰeti.
English: The fire is burning.

h₁sú! h₁éḱwos h₁ōḱús h₁ésti.
English: Good! The horse is swift.

méh₂trs h₂wl̥h₁néh₂ h₁ésti.
English: It is mother's wool.

h₁sú! téwey dómi h₁édmi píboh₂kʷe.
English: Good! I eat and drink in your house.

péḱu h₂éǵrey h₁ésti.
English: The flock is in the field.

só póntoh₂s h₃rēǵós dómom h₁éyti.
English: That road goes to the king's house.

h₂érh₃trom séǵʰoh₂. dwóh₁ gʷówh₁e h₂érh₃troy yunégmi.
English: I hold the plough. I join the two cattle to the plough.

sóh₂wl̥ nókʷti swóm dómom h₁éyti.
English: At night the sun goes to its own house.

Give us great fame.
n̥sméy = to us (dat. pl.); méǵh₂ = great (nom./acc. sg. n.); ḱléwos = fame, glory (acc. sg. n.); dʰedʰh₁dʰí = give! (2sg. imperative)

He slew the serpent.
égʷʰent = (he) struck, slew (3sg. imperfect, augmented); ógʷʰim = serpent, snake (acc. sg.)

The king wanted a son. He asked his priest: "May a son be born to me!" The priest said to the king: "Worship the god Werunos."
h₃rḗḱs = king (nom. sg.); súHnum = son (acc. sg.); wl̥nh₁to = wanted, wished for (3sg. middle imperfect); tósyo = his, of him (gen. sg.); ǵʰéwtorm̥ = priest, pourer of libations (acc. sg.); prēḱst = asked (3sg. aorist); súHnus = son (nom. sg.); moy = to me (dat., enclitic); ǵn̥h₁yetōd = let (him) be born (3sg. future imperative, middle); ǵʰéwtōr = priest (nom. sg.); tom = that, the (acc. sg.); h₃rḗǵm̥ = king (acc. sg.); wewked = said, spoke (3sg. perfect/pluperfect); h₁yáǵeswo = worship, sacrifice to (2sg. middle imperative); deywóm = god (acc. sg.); wérunom = Werunos (acc. sg.)

Good fame.
wésu = good (nom./acc. sg. n.); ḱléwos = fame, glory (nom./acc. sg. n.)

A sheep that had no wool saw horses: one pulling a heavy wagon, one carrying a big load, and one quickly carrying a man.
owis = sheep (nom. sg.); yāi = on which, whose (rel. pron., dat./loc. sg. f.); wl̥nā = wool (nom. sg.); ne = not; eest = was (3sg. imperfect); dedorḱe = saw (3sg. perfect); eḱwons = horses (acc. pl.); tom = the one, that (acc. sg.); woǵʰom = wagon (acc. sg.); gʷr̥um = heavy (acc. sg.); weǵʰontm̥ = pulling, carrying (pres. ppl., acc. sg.); tom = the one (acc. sg.); bʰorom = load (acc. sg.); meǵm̥ = big, great (acc. sg.); tom = the one (acc. sg.); ǵʰm̥onm̥ = man, human (acc. sg.); ōku = quickly; bʰerontm̥ = carrying (pres. ppl., acc. sg.)

Let the word go forth for us.
wékʷos = word, speech (nom. sg. n.); nos = for us, our (enclitic); pró = forth, forward; h₁éytu = let (it) go (3sg. imperative)

Vigorous (sacred) spirit.
ish₁róm = vigorous, mighty, holy (nom./acc. sg. n.); ménos = spirit, mind, force (nom./acc. sg. n.)

Give us imperishable fame.
ń̥dʰgʷʰitom = imperishable, undying (acc. sg. n.); nos = to us (enclitic); ḱléwos = fame, glory (acc. sg. n.); dʰedʰh₁dʰí = give! (2sg. imperative)

"I want a son." "Let it be so," said the bright god Werunos. Then the king's wife bore a son.
súHnum = son (acc. sg.); wēlh₁mi = I want, wish (1sg. present); tód = that (nom./acc. sg. n.); h₁estu = let (it) be (3sg. imperative); wéwked = said (3sg. perfect/pluperfect); lewkós = bright, shining (nom. sg.); deywós = god (nom. sg.); wérunos = Werunos (nom. sg.); nu = now, then; h₃réḱs = of the king (gen. sg.); pótnih₂ = lady, wife (nom. sg.); súHnum = son (acc. sg.); ǵeǵonh₁e = bore, begot (3sg. perfect)

There was a king; he was childless.
h₃rḗḱs = king (nom. sg.); h₁est = was (3sg. imperfect); só = he, that one (nom. sg.); n̥putlós = childless, without sons (nom. sg.)

You lie slain.
gʷʰn̥tṓs = slain, killed (verbal adj., nom. pl.); ḱéydʰwe = you (pl.) lie (2pl. present middle)

"Hear me, father Werunos!" The god Werunos came down from heaven.
ḱludʰí = hear! (2sg. aorist imperative); moi = me (dat., enclitic); pter = father (voc. sg.); werune = Werunos (voc. sg.); deywós = god (nom. sg.); wérunos = Werunos (nom. sg.); diwés = from the sky, heaven (abl./gen. sg.); km̥tá = down; gʷah₂t = came, went (3sg. aorist)
Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field.
The horse said: "Listen, sheep! It pains the heart of us who see it: man, the master, makes the sheep's wool into a warm garment for himself, and the sheep have no wool."
"Let them crush him, let them strike him, and let them put him beneath their own feet."
Having heard this, the sheep fled into the field.
